heroHeadline: Egypt Posts 5.1% Growth for FY2025/26 as Sisi Hosts Greece-Cyprus Summit at El Alamein and Archaeologists Uncover Old Kingdom Judge's Tomb
heroSubtitle: Egypt's Planning Ministry announced on September 3, 2026 that the economy grew 5.1% in fiscal year 2025/26 — up from 4.4% a year earlier and ahead of the IMF's forecast — driven by a 23.3% rebound in Suez Canal revenue and 9% growth in non-oil manufacturing. On September 8, President Sisi hosted Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis and Cypriot President Nikos Christodoulides at El Alamein for the 10th Egypt-Greece-Cyprus Trilateral Summit, where the three leaders backed the Gaza peace plan's second phase, agreed a permanent secretariat in Nicosia, and advanced electricity and gas interconnection projects; the summit coincided with Sisi opening the 2nd El Alamein International Airshow. Separately, an Egyptian-Spanish mission announced the discovery of a 4,300-year-old tomb at Saqqara belonging to Fifth Dynasty judge Yunmen, its wall reliefs still retaining much of their original color.
footerNote: Data sourced from Egyptian official records, UNESCO, academic Egyptology research (Shaw, Lehner, Hawass), major international outlets, IMF, Human Rights Watch, and institutional analyses.
